findings.title: raw_html cook method renders un-sanitized HTML into posts, enabling stored XSS
findings.body: The new `cook_method == :raw_html` path returns `raw` verbatim, completely bypassing the PrettyText/Sanitize pipeline. Feed/import content is user-controlled HTML from an external source (PollFeed does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with no sanitization, and TopicEmbed.import_remote passes Readability output straight through). `scrub` only fixes invalid byte sequences, it does not strip `<script>` or event handlers. The resulting post is then emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb (and anywhere else cooked posts render on the forum domain), so any script in a feed item executes in the forum's origin for every viewer, including logged-in admins. The imported content must be sanitized before being stored/served.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin uses the full referer URL including path, which browsers reject
findings.body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` passes the entire referer URL as the targetOrigin. Per the postMessage spec, targetOrigin must be only scheme://host[:port]; if it contains a path the browser throws a SecurityError (or silently fails in older browsers) and the message is never delivered. Since every real referer includes a path, the 'discourse-resize' message that app/assets/javascripts/embed.js relies on to size the iframe will never arrive, leaving the iframe at its default height. The referer should be reduced to its origin before being used as targetOrigin.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without content
findings.body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls `.scrub` on `i.content` without checking for nil. Many Atom/RSS items only provide a summary/description and no content element, in which case SimpleRSS returns nil and the scheduled job raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire poll (and with retry disabled, nothing is imported until the next run). Guard with something like `(i.content || i.summary || '').scrub`.

findings.title: Origin check uses substring matching instead of strict origin comparison
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any message whose origin appears anywhere inside discourseUrl. This is a fragile check: for example if discourseUrl lacks a trailing slash, an origin like 'https://discourse.example.com' matches even when discourseUrl is 'https://discourse.example.com.evil.tld'-style misconfigurations, and it also matches when the configured URL merely contains the origin as a substring (e.g. discourseUrl '//example.com/path' vs origin 'https://example.com' — inverted cases aside, substring matching is not an origin comparison). Parse both URLs and compare scheme/host/port strictly before resizing the iframe based on a message.

findings.title: TopicEmbed.create! runs even when PostCreator failed to persist the post
findings.body: `creator.create` returns `@post` even when post creation rolled back (e.g. validation or host-spam rollback leaves @post set but not persisted, and in the spam case create swallows the rollback). `post.present?` is then true, so `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: post.topic_id, post_id: post.id)` runs with `post_id = nil` against a `null: false` column (and a possibly nil/unsaved topic_id), raising ActiveRecord::NotNullViolation out of the import path instead of cleanly skipping. Check `post.persisted? && post.errors.blank?` before creating the TopicEmbed.

findings.title: absolutize_urls misses relative URLs that don't start with '/'
findings.body: Only href/src values starting with '/' are rewritten. Relative links like `href="page2.html"` or `src="images/pic.png"` are left untouched, so in imported topics they resolve relative to the forum's domain and produce broken links/images. Use URI.join(url, href) (or equivalent) for any non-absolute URL instead of only root-relative ones.

findings.title: Embedding authorization relies solely on the Referer header host
findings.body: `ensure_embeddable` grants framing based only on `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Direct loads (no referer) are rejected, but referer is client-supplied and can be forged by non-browser clients, and any page on the allowed host — including user-generated content on that host — can embed arbitrary `embed_url` parameters, each enqueueing a retrieve job. The 60s redis throttle in TopicRetriever mitigates volume, but the only thing binding the embed URL to the page is this header check; consider also validating that the embed_url's host matches and documenting that the referer check is not a strong security boundary.
